PullRequest.Title: Reduce motion in session status indicators
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes #342985.

This PR expands the change in #343013 to cover session-status ownership across both session-list surfaces. Thanks to @wasim-builds for the initial motion-reduction work.

## Summary

Flashing input-needed/approval-needed cues and shimmering session names add sustained motion to the session list. This change makes attention cues static while preserving genuine progress animation, and keeps expanded-parent and active-chat status from being mistaken for a child's activity.

## Changes

- Keep input-needed and approval-needed icons and yellow warning fills static in both the Agents Window and the regular workbench Chat Sessions view.
- Remove session-name shimmer in the Agents Window; keep the animated in-progress dot indicator.
- Keep visible child activity on the child while its group is expanded. When collapsed, promote the highest-priority eligible child status to the parent icon, with input needed taking priority over progress.
- Keep the session panel header tied to its active chat, rather than child or side-chat activity.

## Before / After

Matched full-window native Code OSS recordings in **Dark 2026**, using the same scripted sessions and layout. Before restores the pre-change session-status implementation in the same OSS build; After uses this change. Idle pauses are trimmed from the Agents Window clips; playback speed is unchanged.

### Agents Window — motion and parent/child ownership

**Watch:** `04 Parent itself needs approval` keeps a static yellow cue after the change, while `03 Parent itself working` still animates. The completed parents `01` and `02` stay quiet while expanded, then pick up their children's progress or approval icon when collapsed. The sequence finishes by opening the working child and returning to its completed parent; the panel status follows the active chat.

**Before — pulsing attention cues, shimmering working-session names, and aggregate parent status**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3fcff37f-0e0b-462e-9253-92d0fff8e816

**After — static attention cues; child status rolls up only while collapsed; genuine progress remains animated**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0e35dc1-f3c1-4332-8050-90f346bafffb

### Regular workbench — Chat > Sessions

**Watch:** the two approval-needed rows stop pulsing, but `02 Working - progress indicator preserved` continues animating. The completed row stays quiet.

**Before — approval icons and yellow backgrounds pulse**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a18d2f2-80be-46f0-b21b-e46d141bda67

**After — approval icons and yellow backgrounds stay static; progress animation is preserved**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4643807-87ff-4202-becd-80b59df2b34f

## Testing

1. In the Agents Window, use a completed parent with a working child and another completed parent with both an approval-needed child and a working child. Expand both groups: each visible child shows its own status and neither completed parent animates. Collapse the groups: the first parent shows progress, and the second shows approval needed.
2. Open the working child, then return to its completed parent. The panel header reflects the active chat, not activity in another child or side chat.
3. In both the Agents Window and regular workbench Chat > Sessions, leave an approval-needed row and a working row unselected and unhovered. The approval icon and yellow fill remain static; genuine progress continues animating. Hovering or selecting a row still uses the normal row highlight.

Automated validation:

- `scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsList.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\test\browser\sessionHeader.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\test\browser\sessionStatusIcon.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentSessionsViewer.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed; targeted ESLint and stylelint passed.
- [Screenshots & Tests](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39542298318) — passed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Regular workbench Chat > Sessions list rendering and live updates for collapsed multi-chat sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A chat catalog/status observable change synchronously reruns the rendered parent row autoruns. The changed status derivation filters the in-memory chat array, reads eligible child metadata/status, then updates the status icon and may rebuild the small details row before the UI reflects the new roll-up. No asynchronous or remote work blocks progress.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of rendered collapsed sessions multiplied by eligible non-tool chats in each session; list virtualization limits rendered rows, and each child status lifecycle event affects only its owning parent row.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable transactions and autoruns execute serially on the UI thread. There is no parallel fan-out, queue, limiter, or boundary concurrency; multiple status changes in one transaction are coalesced by the observable framework.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session and chat catalog observables are already resident in memory. The changed path does not load chat details and has no cold/warm cache distinction, cache key, negative cache, or coalescing boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the diff adds direct eligible-child subscriptions and linear scans for collapsed rows; low that their realistic magnitude constitutes a performance regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Peer-chat collections are not explicitly capped, so very long-lived sessions could increase observer count and linear scan cost; however, the reviewed code and tests do not establish realistic cardinality or event frequency sufficient to turn these small in-memory scans and row updates into user-visible latency or jank.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The added work is intentional for child-status ownership, remains bounded to rendered rows and in-memory metadata, and lacks evidence of a concrete performance outcome at realistic scale.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expanded multi-chat Sessions rows and session/pane header status updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For expanded rows, the parent derives status from its main chat plus side chats while visible children render their own status. Header updates read only the active chat status/read observables (or constant empty-header defaults) and synchronously update one icon.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One active header and the visible expanded session rows; peer child rows scale with the tree's visible items, while parent aggregation excludes those visible peers when expanded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All reads and DOM/icon updates are synchronous and serialized on the UI thread; no concurrent external operations are started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: All values come from existing observables and the SessionStatusIcon's existing icon cache key. The diff does not alter cache population, invalidation, or miss behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact visible row counts vary, but the changed header path is constant-time and expanded-parent peer aggregation is removed rather than added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The header change narrows reads from aggregate session state to one active chat, and expanded rows avoid rolling visible peer activity into the parent.

Scenarios.Scenario: Needs-input and in-progress visual indicators in the regular Sessions list and Agents Window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: CSS style matching and browser rendering/compositing occur after row class changes. The diff removes infinite icon/background/title animations and removes title registration with the shared progress animation helper; static warning backgrounds and the genuine progress spinner remain.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously visible needs-input or in-progress rows. The previous sustained animation work scaled with those rows; the changed implementation reduces that work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style, paint, and compositor work is browser-managed. The application introduces no new timers, animation loops, or concurrent jobs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is involved; stylesheet rules are loaded once and applied by the browser style engine.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the removed CSS animations and shared title animation registration reduce sustained rendering activity.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact CPU/GPU savings depend on platform and visible row count, but the direction is a reduction in rendering work, not a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. These changes remove ongoing animation work and do not introduce a new performance cost.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 10 changed files and all diff pages. Traced list rendering, reactive child-status aggregation, header updates, and CSS animation changes. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary was introduced or moved onto these paths. The only added scaling work is an in-memory child scan/subscription for collapsed status roll-up; available evidence does not support a concrete user-visible performance regression.
